extracted.intended_audience: American poets, writers, critics, and educated readers interested in the nature and creation of a national literature (late 19th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic guide and set of critical criteria about what should characterize 'American National Literature' and what makes great poetry (voice, maturity, spirit, authenticity). Intended to help writers and critics evaluate or produce enduring, authentically American literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature age as source of transcendent poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps, indeed, the rarest and most blessed quality of transcendent noble poetry ... is, (I would suggest,) from sane, completed, vital, capable old age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that 'completed fruitage' of poetic greatness comes in grand age, the culmination of preceding life; mature experience and 'continuated physiology and psychology' produce the 'aureole' or supreme poetic atmosphere. Implication: value poets' late-life mastery and judge works in the context of long development rather than single early achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final proof of song is matured, diffused atmosphere, not technical feats
rubrics_metrics.description: The final proof of song or personality is a sort of matured, accreted, superb, evoluted, almost divine, impalpable diffuseness and atmosphere or invisible magnetism, dissolving and embracing all--and not any special achievement of passion, pride, metrical form, epigram, plot, thought, or what is call'd beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greatness is judged by an overall pervasive quality or 'magnetism' rather than isolated technical devices or conspicuous effects. Anti-pattern: valuing only metrical cleverness, epigrams, plot twists, or singular passionate moments as proof of lasting poetic worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained physiological and psychological health underpins great art
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed fruitage ... comes (in my opinion) to a grand age ... through an essentially sound continuated physiology and psychology (both important).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay links durable creative power to continued physical and mental soundness across life. Guidance for evaluation: consider the artist's sustained vitality and the health of their sensibility as a factor in producing mature, enduring work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance over generations as test of first-class production
rubrics_metrics.description: Every really first-class production has likely to pass through the crucial tests of a generation, perhaps several generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True literary greatness is confirmed by longevity and changing receptions over time. Expect early hostility to novelty (Voltaire, La Harpe examples) but treat multi-generational acceptance as a strong positive signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect initial resistance to novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: People resent anything new as a personal insult. ... Voltaire term'd the Shaksperean works 'a huge dunghill' ... One of the prevalent objections ... was ... that if a ship should reach India she would never get back again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: innovators should anticipate hostile early criticism; critics should factor in conservative bias when judging new work. Historical examples are given to show that ridicule often precedes recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity/autocthony: national literature must arise from its own soil and soul
rubrics_metrics.description: One part of the national American literatus's task is ... to be devoted to and exploit our own day, its diffused light, freedom, responsibilities, with all it necessitates ... autochthonic song, and how for a really great people there can be no complete and glorious Name, short of emerging out of and even rais'd on such born poetic expression, coming from its own soil and soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American literature should grow organically from the country's own experiences, idioms, and character rather than merely imitating foreign models. Advice to writers: mine native materials, landscapes, people, and democratic life for authentic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble/collective formation is the tap-root of national literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble is the tap-root of National Literature. America is become already a huge world of peoples ... and (I predict) a yet to be National Literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National literature emerges from the combined voices and experiences of many regions and peoples, not from a single metropolitan school. Anti-pattern: allowing a few coastal cities or a narrow elite to monopolize the definition of national literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: National literature should reflect the people 'en masse' and prevailing traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Books too reflect humanity _en masse_, and surely show them splendidly, or the reverse, and prove or celebrate their prevalent traits (these last the main things.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgment should consider how well works mirror the character and common life of the nation (its 'prevalent traits'), since books are signs of a nation's deeper condition. Guidance for creators: attend to communal realities and shared temperaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired national traits to appear in literature: Good-Nature, Decorum, Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: When I have had a chance ... I have invariably found coming to the front three prevailing personal traits, to be named here for brevity's sake under the heads Good-Nature, Decorum, and Intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer recommends these three qualities as the 'vertebral stock' of the nation's finest character and as bases to be embodied in national literature. Use them as evaluative criteria for tone and spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noblesse Oblige: literature and public life should express moral responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: My opinion is that this foregoing phrase, and its spirit, should influence and permeate official America ... should be one of their chiefest mottoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature ought to reflect and encourage an ethic of responsibility and uplift—'noblesse oblige' for a nation as well as individuals. Creators should aim for moral largeness rather than petty vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand spiritual scope: include evil and criminals within a larger Deific identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The expanded scientific and democratic and truly philosophic and poetic quality of modernism demands a Deific identity and scope superior to all limitations, and essentially including just as well the so-call'd evil and crime and criminals--all the malformations, the defective and abortions of the universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature's spiritual vision should be broad and inclusive, willing to comprehend moral complexity and not shrink from the presence of evil; modern writers should give philosophical breadth rather than narrow moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subtle allusion and hidden hints to engage the discerning reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the bulk of the common people ... relish a well-hidden allusion or hint carelessly dropt, faintly indicated, and left to be disinterr'd or not. ... It is always a capital compliment from author to reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ tasteful, faintly indicated allusions as a way to reward perceptive readers and create layers of meaning. Guidance: subtlety can be a positive artistic device when used judiciously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patriotism, Nationality, and Ensemble should be deep and genuine (not mere bragging)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are now deepest wanted in the States as roots for their literature are Patriotism, Nationality, Ensemble, or the ideas of these, and the uncompromising genesis and saturation of these. Not the mere bawling and braggadocio of them, but the radical emotion-facts, the fervor and perennial fructifying spirit at fountain-head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate patriotic content by its sincerity, depth, and capacity to fertilize long-term literary growth; avoid superficial or boastful nationalisms. Writers should cultivate genuine emotional roots rather than rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid narrow puritanical standards for national literature
rubrics_metrics.description: For this vast and varied Commonwealth, geographically and artistically, the puritanical standards are constipated, narrow, and non-philosophic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author counsels against letting Puritan-derived narrowness dominate literary standards; encourage breadth, philosophical depth, and aesthetic freedom instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity of printed matter does not equal true literature
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not follow, because the United States print and read more books, magazines, and newspapers than all the rest of the world, that they really have therefore a literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate mass publication and high circulation with genuine literary achievement. Evaluators should emphasize quality and depth over volume and surface proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace evolutionary development; literature must reflect modern evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The great current points are perhaps simple, after all: first, that the highest developments of the New World and Democracy, and probably the best society of the civilized world all over, are to be only reach'd and spinally nourish'd (in my notion) by a new evolutionary sense and treatment; and, secondly, that the evolution-principle ... has now reach'd us markedly for and in our literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should adopt an evolutionary, progressive sensibility—responding to scientific and democratic changes—and critics should value works that embody that modernizing impulse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance respect for heritage with devotion to present-day life
rubrics_metrics.description: One part of the national American literatus's task is (and it is not an easy one) to treat the old hereditaments, legends, poems, theologies, and even customs, with fitting respect and toleration, and at the same time clearly understand and justify, and be devoted to and exploit our own day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should neither slavishly imitate the past nor dismiss it; instead show respectful handling of traditions while actively exploring contemporary themes and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek simple, natural health and first-hand power in literary production
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest feature in current poetry (perhaps in literature anyhow) is the almost total lack of first-class power, and simple, natural health, flourishing and produced at first hand, typifying our own era. Modern verse generally lacks quite altogether the modern, and is oftener possess'd in spirit with the past and feudal, dressed may-be in late fashions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize works that feel vital, healthy, and directly born of present experience rather than morbid, derivative, or feudal-tinged pastiches. Anti-pattern: valuing vogueish past styles over authentic contemporary spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: American poetry should be spiritual and democratic (future-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Old World ... is the region of the poetry of concrete and real things,--the past, the esthetic, palaces, etiquette ... But the New World (America) is the region of the future, and its poetry must be spiritual and democratic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should orient toward democratic ideals and broadened spiritual concerns—addressing future-facing themes rather than reproducing Old-World aesthetic preoccupations; critics should reward that orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The human voice (timbre) is a central cultivated instrument for poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Stating it briefly and pointedly I should suggest that the human voice is a cultivation or form'd growth on a fair native foundation. ... Beyond all other power and beauty, there is something in the quality and power of the right voice (_timbre_ the schools call it) that touches the soul, the abysms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For delivery and oral power, value physiological voice quality and cultivated timbre; the voice can rouse or reveal poetry in ways the written page alone cannot. Advice: cultivate vocal technique on a native physiological basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science is the final critic and poetry must reckon with scientific-modern outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Then science, the final critic of all, has the casting vote for future poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern literature should not ignore scientific thought; its insights and outlook should inform and test poetic claims. Evaluators should consider compatibility with contemporary scientific and intellectual developments.
